title: Lonely numbers
_map: Lonely numbers (stretch). Big idea: some numbers (7, 11, 13) only make one row: prime numbers. Creative: find all the lonely numbers up to 30 using chickens.
_story: New chickens hatch: 7 of them. They try to line up in equal rows like the 12 did, but it never works. Ismaeel discovers 'lonely' numbers, names them primes, and Steve claims 9 is lonely.
_stepChain: arrays (rows-of-chickens) → 12 makes many arrays → 7 only makes one long row → numbers like that are called prime → test 11 → Steve thinks 9 is prime → hunt up to 30

talk.goodAnswer: 7 chickens can only make one row of 7 (or 7 rows of 1); any other number of rows leaves some over. That makes it prime.

talk.ask: Is 9 lonely? How do you know?

handsOn: Take 11 Lego bricks. Try to make equal rows. Then try 12. Which number makes more arrays? Can you find another lonely number?

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Seven new chicks hatched! They want to line up in equal rows like the big chickens. But they keep getting into a muddle.
Try different numbers of rows for 7 chicks. Which ones work with nobody left over?
7 only works as one long row, or every chick on its own. Any other number of rows leaves chicks over. A lonely number like that, that only makes one row, is called a prime number.
Let's test 11. Can 11 chicks make any equal rows, apart from one long row?

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: I think 9 is a lonely number too! It's odd, and it feels lonely.

question.onRight: Yes, you caught it. 9 makes 3 rows of 3, so it isn't lonely.

0.mistake: thinks odd numbers are always prime
0.hint: Try 3 rows. Do 9 chicks fit with none left over?
0.say: Being odd doesn't make a number lonely. 9 chicks make 3 rows of 3, with none left over. So 9 isn't prime.

question.reveal: 9 is 3 rows of 3. Not lonely at all!

narration.text: The lonely numbers up to 30 are: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23 and 29. Mathematicians have been hunting for bigger and bigger lonely numbers for thousands of years, and they never run out.

rule.text: A prime number only makes one row.
rule.ask: Can you say what makes a number lonely? Say it out loud. Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: A prime number, a lonely number, can only make one row. Any other rows leave some left over.

bonus.reveal: Mathematicians decided 1 isn't a prime number. It's a special number of its own. Even mathematicians had to agree on a rule for that one!
